# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer RS256-signed JWT access token signed with your registered private key.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer SSO bearer token.

<h1 id="ib-rest-api-account-management-accounts">Account Management Accounts</h1>

## Retrieve Processed Application

<a id="opIdlistAccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/accounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /gw/api/v1/accounts`

Retrieve the application request and IBKR response data based on IBKR accountId or externalId. Only available for accounts that originate via API<br><br>**Scope**: `accounts.read`<br>**Security Policy**: `HTTPS`

<h3 id="retrieve-processed-application-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|query|string|false|none|
|externalId|query|string|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accountId": "string",
  "requestFileName": "string",
  "responseFileName": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "http://example.com",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 0,
  "detail": "string",
  "instance": "http://example.com"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "http://example.com",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 0,
  "detail": "string",
  "instance": "http://example.com"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "http://example.com",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 0,
  "detail": "string",
  "instance": "http://example.com"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "type": "http://example.com",
  "title": "string",
  "status": 0,
  "detail": "string",
  "instance": "http://example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-processed-application-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Retrieve the application request and IBKR response data based on IBKR accountId or externalId. Only available for accounts that originate via API|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returns error description representing bad request|[ProblemDetailResponse](#schemaproblemdetailresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returns error description representing access issue|[ProblemDetailResponse](#schemaproblemdetailresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns error description representing access issue|[ProblemDetailResponse](#schemaproblemdetailresponse)|
|415|Unsupported Media Type|Unsupported Media Type|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Returns error description representing internal server error|[ProblemDetailResponse](#schemaproblemdetailresponse)|

<h3 id="retrieve-processed-application-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[FileDetailsResponse](#schemafiledetailsresponse)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[ResponseFileResponse](#schemaresponsefileresponse)|false|none|none|

Status Code **415**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2Bearer
</aside>

## Submit General Agreements And Disclosures

<a id="opIdcreateAccountsDocuments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/accounts/documents \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/jwt' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"processDocuments":{"documents":[{"signedBy":"Jane L Doe","attachedFile":{"fileName":"Form5001.pdf","fileLength":432177,"sha1Checksum":"03D899BA757F617C907A1F021D7046AC1DAC8707"},"formNumber":0,"validAddress":true,"execLoginTimestamp":-1186971863,"execTimestamp":-1186971863,"documentType":"Brokerage Statement","signature":"string","externalAccountId":"string","externalIndividualId":"Test_22","proofOfIdentityType":"Driver License","expirationDate":"1970-01-01","proofOfAddressType":"Bank Statement","payload":{"mimeType":"application/pdf","data":"pm.collectionVariables.get('\''form5001'\'')"}}],"inputLanguage":"en","translation":true}}'
```

`POST /gw/api/v1/accounts/documents`

Provides mechanism to submit Agreements and Disclosures to IBKR once a day instead of with each application. We store these documents on the servers and will use them for new application requests submitted that day.<ul><li>Documents will need to be submitted once a day (before the Applications are submitted). PDFs will be displayed and submitted as is- no changes/edits will be made to the actual PDF files.</li><li>This end-point will not process any Tax Form Documents. Tax Form document should be submitted with every application</li><li>If submitted in the morning, you only need to include the Tax Form attachment for each applicant. Otherwise, you will need to include PDFs with each application (Create Account).</li></ul><br><br>**Scope**: `accounts.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "processDocuments": {
    "documents": [
      {
        "signedBy": "Jane L Doe",
        "attachedFile": {
          "fileName": "Form5001.pdf",
          "fileLength": 432177,
          "sha1Checksum": "03D899BA757F617C907A1F021D7046AC1DAC8707"
        },
        "formNumber": 0,
        "validAddress": true,
        "execLoginTimestamp": -1186971863,
        "execTimestamp": -1186971863,
        "documentType": "Brokerage Statement",
        "signature": "string",
        "externalAccountId": "string",
        "externalIndividualId": "Test_22",
        "proofOfIdentityType": "Driver License",
        "expirationDate": "1970-01-01",
        "proofOfAddressType": "Bank Statement",
        "payload": {
          "mimeType": "application/pdf",
          "data": "pm.collectionVariables.get('form5001')"
        }
      }
    ],
    "inputLanguage": "en",
    "translation": true
  }
}
```

<a id="opIdupdateAccountsTasks"></a>

## Manage Bank Instructions

<a id="opIdcreateBankInstructions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/bank-instructions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "instructionType": "ACH_INSTRUCTION",
    "instruction": {
      "clientInstructionId": 1012983,
      "bankInstructionCode": "USACH",
      "achType": "DEBIT_CREDIT",
      "bankInstructionName": "TestInstr",
      "currency": "USD",
      "accountId": "U223454",
      "clientAccountInfo": {
        "bankRoutingNumber": "202012983",
        "bankAccountNumber": "101267576983",
        "bankName": "JPM Chase",
        "bankAccountTypeCode": 0
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /gw/api/v1/bank-instructions`

Create or delete bank instructions by accountId. ACH, Open Banking, Withdrawal (against an existing Open Banking deposit), Traditional Bank Instruction Verification, Predefined Destination, and eDDA are supported for 'Create'.<br><br>**Scope**: `bank-instructions.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "instructionType": "ACH_INSTRUCTION",
  "instruction": {
    "clientInstructionId": 1012983,
    "bankInstructionCode": "USACH",
    "achType": "DEBIT_CREDIT",
    "bankInstructionName": "TestInstr",
    "currency": "USD",
    "accountId": "U223454",
    "clientAccountInfo": {
      "bankRoutingNumber": "202012983",
      "bankAccountNumber": "101267576983",
      "bankName": "JPM Chase",
      "bankAccountTypeCode": 0
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="manage-bank-instructions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client-id|path|string|true|The client's clientId|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» instructionType|body|string|true|none|
|» instruction|body|[TraditionalBankInstructionVerification](#schematraditionalbankinstructionverification) \| [AchInstruction](#schemaachinstruction) \| [OpenBankingInstruction](#schemaopenbankinginstruction) \| [WithdrawalBankInstruction](#schemawithdrawalbankinstruction) \| [DeleteBankInstruction](#schemadeletebankinstruction) \| [PredefinedDestinationInstruction](#schemapredefineddestinationinstruction) \| [EddaInstruction](#schemaeddainstruction)|true|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[TraditionalBankInstructionVerification](#schematraditionalbankinstructionverification)|false|Request to verify a pending bank instruction using micro-deposit amounts.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[AchInstruction](#schemaachinstruction)|false|Request to create an ACH bank instruction linking an external US or Canada bank account.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[OpenBankingInstruction](#schemaopenbankinginstruction)|false|Request to link a bank account via an open banking provider.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[WithdrawalBankInstruction](#schemawithdrawalbankinstruction)|false|Request to create a withdrawal bank instruction based on an existing deposit link.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[DeleteBankInstruction](#schemadeletebankinstruction)|false|Request to delete a saved bank instruction.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[PredefinedDestinationInstruction](#schemapredefineddestinationinstruction)|false|Request to create a predefined withdrawal destination bank instruction.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[EddaInstruction](#schemaeddainstruction)|false|Request to set up an electronic Direct Debit Authorization (eDDA) bank instruction.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» instructionType|OPEN_BANKING_INSTRUCTION|
|» instructionType|WITHDRAWAL_INSTRUCTION|

|» instructionType|DELETE_BANK_INSTRUCTION|
|» instructionType|PREDEFINED_DESTINATION_INSTRUCTION|
|» instructionType|EDDA_INSTRUCTION|

`POST /gw/api/v1/external-asset-transfers`

Initiate request to submit external position transfer. Methods- ACATS, ATON, Basic FOP, FOP, DWAC. More information on transfer methods can be found here - https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/trading-lessons/cash-and-position-transfers/<br><br>**Scope**: `transfers.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "instructionType": "FOP",
  "instruction": {
    "clientInstructionId": 7013038,
    "direction": "IN",
    "accountId": "U46377",
    "contraBrokerAccountId": "12345678A",
    "contraBrokerDtcCode": "534",
    "quantity": 1000,
    "tradingInstrument": {
      "conid": 12123,
      "currency": "USD"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="transfer-positions-externally-acats-aton-fop-dwac-complex-asset-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client-id|path|string|true|The client's clientId|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» instructionType|body|string|true|none|
|» instruction|body|[FopInstruction](#schemafopinstruction) \| [DwacInstruction](#schemadwacinstruction) \| [ComplexAssetTransferInstruction](#schemacomplexassettransferinstruction) \| [ExternalPositionTransfer](#schemaexternalpositiontransfer) \| [IsaTransferInstruction](#schemaisatransferinstruction)|true|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[FopInstruction](#schemafopinstruction)|false|Request to transfer a position free of payment (FOP).|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[DwacInstruction](#schemadwacinstruction)|false|Request to transfer a position via DWAC (Deposit/Withdrawal At Custodian).|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ComplexAssetTransferInstruction](#schemacomplexassettransferinstruction)|false|Request to transfer positions to or from a contra broker (Basic FOP / complex asset transfer, v2). Basic FOP (Free of Payment) transfers assets from financial institutions generally outside the US (equities, fixed income, structured products, options); IBKR coordinates settlement instructions with the institution.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[ExternalPositionTransfer](#schemaexternalpositiontransfer)|false|Request to transfer positions from an external broker via ACATS or ATON.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[IsaTransferInstruction](#schemaisatransferinstruction)|false|Request to transfer a UK ISA to Interactive Brokers from another ISA provider.|

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Generates Statements In Supported Formats Based On Request Parameters.

<a id="opIdcreateStatements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/statements \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "UXXXX",
    "startDate": "20230102",
    "endDate": "20230102",
    "mimeType": "text/html"
  }'
```

`POST /gw/api/v1/statements`

<br>**Scope**: `statements.read` OR `statements.write` OR `reports.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accountId": "UXXXX",
  "startDate": "20230102",
  "endDate": "20230102",
  "mimeType": "text/html"
}
```

<h3 id="generates-statements-in-supported-formats-based-on-request-parameters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorization|header|string|true|Specifies the authorization header value (e.g., Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1...).|
|body|body|[StmtRequest](#schemastmtrequest)|true|Report request object|
|» accountId|body|string|true|account id|
|» accountIds|body|[string]|false|array of account id's|
|» startDate|body|string|true|from date|
|» endDate|body|string|true|to date|
|» multiAccountFormat|body|string|false|possible values are consolidate, concatenate, or customConsolidate|
|» cryptoConsolIfAvailable|body|boolean|false|crypto consolidate flag, If request contains any accounts with crypto segment, will turn request into Crypto Consolidated|
|» mimeType|body|string|false|output format|
|» language|body|string|false|two character ISO language code|
|» gzip|body|boolean|false|to gzip the whole response pass true|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "dataType": "string",
    "encoding": "string",
    "value": "string",
```

<h1 id="ib-rest-api-authorization-sso-browser-sessions">Authorization SSO Browser Sessions</h1>

## Create SSO Browser Session.

<a id="opIdcreateSsoBrowserSessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/sso-browser-sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/jwt' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"credential":"ddowney2","ip":"10.10.10.10"}'
```

`POST /gw/api/v1/sso-browser-sessions`

<br>**Scope**: `sso-browser-sessions.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "credential": "ddowney2",
  "ip": "10.10.10.10"
}
```

<h3 id="create-sso-browser-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|authorization|header|string|true|Specifies the authorization header value (e.g., Bearer eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1...).|
|body|body|[CreateBrowserSessionRequest](#schemacreatebrowsersessionrequest)|true|Create browser session on behalf of end-user.|
|» credential|body|string|true|none|
|» ip|body|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "url": "https://www.interactivebrokers.com/sso/..."
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "type": "/invalid-argument",
  "title": "Bad Request",
  "status": 400,
  "invalidArguments": [
    {
      "field": "accountId",
      "description": "Missing required parameter"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "type": "/simple",
  "title": "Unauthorized",
  "status": 401,
  "detail": "The access token request is invalid"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "type": "/simple",
  "title": "Forbidden",
  "status": 403,
  "detail": "The access token fails to have sufficient scope"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "type": "/simple",
  "title": "Internal Server Error",
  "status": 500
}
```

<h3 id="create-sso-browser-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Create a Single Sign On (SSO) to access the IBKR hosted portal (White Branded).|[CreateBrowserSessionResponse](#schemacreatebrowsersessionresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns a Problem detail instance representing a bad request.|[MissingRequiredParameterResponse](#schemamissingrequiredparameterresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returns a Problem detail instance representing an unauthorized request.|[InvalidAccessTokenResponse](#schemainvalidaccesstokenresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns a Problem detail instance representing a forbidden request.|[InsufficientScopeResponse](#schemainsufficientscoperesponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Returns a Problem detail instance representing an internal server error.|[InternalServerErrorResponse](#schemainternalservererrorresponse)|

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{"credential":"ddowney2","ip":"10.10.10.10","service":"string","alternativeIps":["10.10.10.11","10.10.10.12"]}'
```

`POST /gw/api/v1/sso-sessions`

<br>**Scope**: `sso-sessions.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

```json
{
  "credential": "ddowney2",
  "ip": "10.10.10.10",
  "service": "string",
  "alternativeIps": [
    "10.10.10.11",
```

|body|body|[CreateSessionRequest](#schemacreatesessionrequest)|true|Create session on behalf of end-user.|
|» credential|body|string|true|none|
|» ip|body|string|true|none|
|» service|body|string|false|none|
|» alternativeIps|body|[string]|false|none|

```json
    {
      "field": "accountId",

    }
```

<h1 id="ib-rest-api-pretrade-compliance-restrictions">PreTrade Compliance Restrictions</h1>

## Apply PTC CSV

<a id="opIdapplyCSV"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/restrictions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d 'eyJ0eXAiOiJhdCtKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjFkOTEx...'
```

`POST /gw/api/v1/restrictions`

Applies previously verified CSV changes. Requires two tokens:

**Authorization header** — RS256-signed JWT containing an `accountId` claim, used to identify the master account. A missing or invalid token does not return HTTP 401; the request proceeds and fails at validation with `success: false`.

**Request body** — a separate RS256-signed JWT (validity: 1 minute) whose payload contains the request claims (`userName`, `requestId`, `payload`, and optionally `isEmpTrack`). The `requestId` must match a prior successful `/csv/v2/verify` call.

Failures that occur before the body JWT payload is parsed (inactive token, missing payload) return `success: false` without a `requestId` field.<br><br>**Scope**: `restrictions.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

> Body parameter

```text
eyJ0eXAiOiJhdCtKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjFkOTEx...
```

<h3 id="apply-ptc-csv-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|RS256-signed JWT (Bearer format), signed with your registered private key. Must contain an `accountId` claim identifying the master account. Separate from and additional to the JWT in the request body.|
|body|body|string(jwt)|true|RS256-signed JWT (validity: 1 minute) whose payload contains `userName`, `requestId`, `payload` (Base64-encoded CSV), and optionally `isEmpTrack`. The `requestId` must match a prior successful `/csv/v2/verify` call. Distinct from the Authorization header JWT.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "requestId": 1,
  "message": "OK"
}
```

<h3 id="apply-ptc-csv-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Always HTTP 200. Inspect the `success` field to determine the outcome. All failure conditions — authentication, authorization, validation, and internal errors — return `success: false`.|[CSVResponse](#schemacsvresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2Bearer
</aside>

## Verify PTC CSV

<a id="opIdverifyCSV"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/restrictions/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d 'eyJ0eXAiOiJhdCtKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjFkOTEx...'
```

`POST /gw/api/v1/restrictions/verify`

Validates CSV content without applying changes. Must be called before `/csv/v2/apply` with the same `requestId`.

The master account identity is resolved from the `accountId` claim in the Authorization header JWT. Do not include `masterAcctId` in the request body.

A missing or invalid Authorization header does not return HTTP 401. The request proceeds and fails at validation with `success: false, message: "Master account not specified and not emp track"` unless `isEmpTrack: T` is set in the body.<br><br>**Scope**: `restrictions.write`<br>**Security Policy**: `Signed JWT`

> Body parameter

```text
eyJ0eXAiOiJhdCtKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjFkOTEx...
```

<h3 id="verify-ptc-csv-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|RS256-signed JWT (Bearer format), signed with your registered private key. Must contain an `accountId` claim identifying the master account.|
|body|body|string(jwt)|true|RS256-signed JWT whose payload contains `userName`, `requestId`, and Base64-encoded CSV `payload`. Do not include `masterAcctId`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "requestId": 1,
  "message": "OK"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-ptc-csv-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Always HTTP 200. Inspect the `success` field to determine the outcome. All failure conditions — authentication, authorization, validation, and internal errors — return `success: false`.|[CSVResponse](#schemacsvresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
oauth2Bearer
</aside>

`GET /gw/api/v1/restrictions/account`

Returns all restriction IDs for the given account. The account must be the caller's master account or a direct sub-account. Returns 403 for both unauthorized and non-existent accounts to prevent ID enumeration.<br><br>**Scope**: `restrictions.read`<br>**Security Policy**: `HTTPS`

|masterUserName|query|string|true|IBKR master username of the authenticated caller. Max 64 characters.|
|accountId|query|string|true|Master or sub-account ID. Max 64 characters.|
|isEmpTrack|query|string|false|Set to `T` for employer-track authorization.|

```json
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

```json
  "statusCode": 403
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
  "statusCode": 500
}
```

|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Resource does not belong to the caller, does not exist, or an unsupported HTTP method was used. All cases return an identical body to prevent ID enumeration.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

<h3 id="get-restriction-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Get Restriction Scope

<a id="opIdgetRestrictionScope"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.ibkr.com/gw/api/v1/restrictions/restriction-scope?masterUserName=user1&restrictionId=1001' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /gw/api/v1/restrictions/restriction-scope`

Returns a restriction's scope (`Active For Family`, `Active Except`, `Active For Some`, or `Inactive`) and the account IDs relevant to that scope. `accountIds` is omitted for `Active For Family` and `Inactive` (implicit: all/no accounts). For `Active For Some`, `accountIds` is capped at a configurable limit (default 10000) with a `truncated` flag indicating whether more accounts exist beyond the cap. For `Active Except`, `accountIds` (the excluded accounts) is always returned in full, uncapped. The restriction must be owned by the caller's master account. Employee-track (`isEmpTrack=T`) callers are not supported.<br><br>**Scope**: `restrictions.read`<br>**Security Policy**: `HTTPS`

<h3 id="get-restriction-scope-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Authorization|header|string|true|RS256-signed JWT (Bearer format), signed with your registered private key. Must contain an `accountId` claim identifying the master account. A missing or invalid token returns HTTP 401.|
|masterUserName|query|string|true|IBKR master username of the authenticated caller. Max 64 characters.|
|restrictionId|query|integer(int64)|true|Positive integer. Decimals and non-numeric values return 400.|
|isEmpTrack|query|string|false|Set to `T` for employer-track authorization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "restrictionId": 1001,
  "scope": "Active For Family"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Bad Request: Missing required param: userName",
  "statusCode": 400
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Access denied",
  "statusCode": 403
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "There was an error processing the request. Please try again.",
  "statusCode": 500
}
```

<h3 id="get-restriction-scope-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Restriction scope and relevant account IDs.|[RestrictionScopeResponse](#schemarestrictionscoperesponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Missing, empty, non-numeric, or out-of-range parameter. The `error` field is always prefixed with `Bad Request:`.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|Resource does not belong to the caller, does not exist, or an unsupported HTTP method was used. All cases return an identical body to prevent ID enumeration.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal server error.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

oauth2Bearer
</aside>

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

<h1 id="ib-rest-api-trading-alerts">Trading Alerts</h1>

## Create Or Modify Alert

<a id="opIdcreateAlert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/iserver/account/U1234567/alert \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "alertName": "AAPL_Price",
    "alertMessage": "AAPL Price Drop!",
    "alertRepeatable": 0,
    "email": "jonh.smith@example.com",
    "expireTime": "20231231-12:00:00",
    "iTWSOrdersOnly": 0,
    "outsideRth": 0,
    "sendMessage": 1,
    "showPopup": 1,
    "tif": "GTC",
    "conditions": [
      {
        "conidex": "265598@NYSE",
        "logicBind": "a",
        "operator": ">=",
        "timeZone": "US/Eastern",
        "triggerMethod": "0",
        "type": 1,
        "value": "500"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/iserver/account/{accountId}/alert`

Endpoint used to create a new alert, or modify an existing alert.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alertName": "AAPL_Price",
  "alertMessage": "AAPL Price Drop!",
  "alertRepeatable": 0,
  "email": "jonh.smith@example.com",
  "expireTime": "20231231-12:00:00",
  "iTWSOrdersOnly": 0,
  "outsideRth": 0,
  "sendMessage": 1,
  "showPopup": 1,
  "tif": "GTC",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "conidex": "265598@NYSE",
      "logicBind": "a",
      "operator": ">=",
      "timeZone": "US/Eastern",
      "triggerMethod": "0",
      "type": 1,
      "value": "500"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-modify-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[alertCreationRequest](#schemaalertcreationrequest)|true|none|
|» orderId|body|integer(int64)|false|optional; used in case of modification and represent Alert Id|
|» alertName|body|string|true|Alert name.|
|» alertMessage|body|string|true|Alert message which will be sent|
|» alertRepeatable|body|integer(int64)|true|Boolean number (0, 1) signifies if an alert can be triggered more than once. A value of '1' is required for MTA alerts|
|» email|body|string|false|Email address you want to send email alerts to|
|» expireTime|body|string|false|Used with a tif of "GTD" only. Signifies time when the alert should terminate if no alert is triggered.|
|» iTWSOrdersOnly|body|integer(int64)|false|allow (0) or disallow (1) alerts to trigger alerts through the mobile app|
|» outsideRth|body|integer(int64)|true|Allow (1) or disallow (0) the alert to be triggered outside of regular trading hours|
|» sendMessage|body|integer(int64)|false|allow (1) or disallow (0) alerts to trigger email messages|
|» showPopup|body|integer(int64)|false|allow (1) or disallow (0) alerts to trigger TWS Pop-up messages|
|» tif|body|string|true|Time in Force duration of alert.|
|» conditions|body|[object]|true|Container for all conditions applied for an alert to trigger.|
|» » conidex|body|string|true|Concatenation of conid and exchange. Formatted as "conid@exchange"|
|» » logicBind|body|string|true|Describes how multiple conditions should behave together. Available logic types:<br>  * `a` - AND<br>  * `o` - OR<br>  * `n` - END<br>|
|» » operator|body|string|true|Indicates whether the trigger should be above or below the given value.|
|» » timeZone|body|string|false|Only needed for some MTA alert condition.|
|» » triggerMethod|body|string|true|Pass the string representation of zero, "0"|
|» » type|body|integer(int64)|true|Designate what condition type to use. Note the "MTA" types listed are only supported if iTWSOrdersOnly=1 Available condition types:<br>  * `1` - Price<br>  * `3` - Time<br>  * `4` - Margin<br>  * `5` - Trade<br>  * `6` - Volume<br>  * `7` - MTA Market<br>  * `8` - MTA Postion<br>  * `9` - MTA Account Daily PnL<br>|
|» » value|body|string|true|Trigger value based on Type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» alertRepeatable|0|
|» alertRepeatable|1|
|» outsideRth|0|
|» outsideRth|1|
|» sendMessage|0|
|» sendMessage|1|
|» tif|GTC|
|» tif|GTD|
|» » logicBind|a|
|» » logicBind|o|
|» » logicBind|n|
|» » operator|>=|
|» » operator|<=|
|» » operator|>|
|» » operator|<|
|» » operator|==|
|» » type|1|
|» » type|3|
|» » type|4|
|» » type|5|
|» » type|6|
|» » type|7|
|» » type|8|
|» » type|9|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": null,
  "order_id": 1408549184,
  "success": true,
  "text": "Submitted",
  "order_status": null,
  "warning_message": null
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Bad Request: body can't be empty",
  "statusCode": 400
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Condition #1:can't recognize fix [abc]"
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "statusCode": 0
}
```

<h3 id="create-or-modify-alert-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|An object containing valid accounts and the account properties regarding trading access. This endpoint is also used to confirm account validation.|[alertCreationResponse](#schemaalertcreationresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|bad request; body is empty|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error. Unable to process request if incoming values are not valid. For example operator is "abc" Or if modification request contains unmodified fields<br>|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|service is unavailable. For example if request takes more than 10s due to some internal service unavailability,  request aborted and this status returned<br>|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ssoBearer
</aside>

## Activate Or Deactivate An Alert

<a id="opIdactivateAlert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/iserver/account/U1234567/alert/activate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "alertId": 9876543210,
    "alertActive": 1
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/iserver/account/{accountId}/alert/activate`

Activate or Deactivate existing alerts created for this account. This does not delete alerts, but disables notifications until reactivated.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alertId": 9876543210,
  "alertActive": 1
}
```

<h3 id="activate-or-deactivate-an-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[alertActivationRequest](#schemaalertactivationrequest)|true|none|
|» alertId|body|integer(int64)|true|The alert Identifier|
|» alertActive|body|integer(int64)|true|Set whether or not the alert should be active (1) or inactive (0).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» alertActive|1|
|» alertActive|0|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "request_id": null,
  "order_id": 833967258,
  "success": true,
  "text": "Request was submitted",
  "failure_list": null
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "failed to activate/deactivate alert"
}
```

<h3 id="activate-or-deactivate-an-alert-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|An object containing details about the activated/deactivated alert.|[alertActivationResponse](#schemaalertactivationresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error; unable to process incoming request due to invalid data in it|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ssoBearer
</aside>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cfi_code|string|false|none|Classification of Financial Instrument codes|
|symbol|string|false|none|Underlying symbol|
|cusip|string \| null|false|none|Returns the CUSIP for the given instrument. Only used in BOND trading.|
|expiry_full|string|false|none|Returns the expiration month of the contract.|
|con_id|integer(int64)|false|none|Indicates the contract identifier of the given contract.|
|maturity_date|string|false|none|Indicates the final maturity date of the given contract.|
|industry|string|false|none|Specific group of companies or businesses.|
|instrument_type|string|false|none|Asset class of the instrument.|
|trading_class|string|false|none|Designated trading class of the contract.|
|valid_exchanges|string|false|none|Comma separated list of support exchanges or trading venues.|
|allow_sell_long|boolean|false|none|Allowed to sell shares you own.|
|is_zero_commission_security|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the contract supports zero commission trading.|
|local_symbol|string|false|none|Contract's symbol from primary exchange. For options it is the OCC symbol.|
|contract_clarification_type|string|false|none|none|
|classifier|string|false|none|none|
|currency|string|false|none|Base currency contract is traded in.|
|text|string|false|none|Indicates the display name of the contract, as shown with Client Portal.|
|underlying_con_id|integer(int64)|false|none|Underlying contract identifier for the requested contract.|
|r_t_h|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the contract can be traded outside regular trading hours or not.|
|multiplier|string|false|none|Indicates the multiplier of the contract.|
|underlying_issuer|string|false|none|Indicates the issuer of the underlying.|
|contract_month|string|false|none|Indicates the year and month the contract expires.|
|company_name|string|false|none|Indicates the name of the company or index.|
|smart_available|boolean|false|none|Indicates if the contract can be smart routed or not.|
|exchange|string|false|none|Indicates the primary exchange for which the contract can be traded.|
|category|string|false|none|Indicates the industry category of the instrument.|
|rules|[contractRules](#schemacontractrules)|false|none|detailed contract information|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ssoBearer
</aside>

## List All Stock Conids By Exchange

<a id="opIdgetConidsByExchange"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/trsrv/all-conids?exchange=AMEX' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/api/trsrv/all-conids`

Send out a request to retrieve all contracts made available on a requested exchange. This returns all contracts that are tradable on the exchange, even those that are not using the exchange as their primary listing.

<h3 id="list-all-stock-conids-by-exchange-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exchange|query|string|true|none|
|assetClass|query|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "ticker": "BMO",
    "conid": 5094,
    "exchange": "NYSE"
  },
  {
    "ticker": "BNS",
    "conid": 15156975,
    "exchange": "NYSE"
  }
]
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string"
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "statusCode": 0
}
```

<h3 id="list-all-stock-conids-by-exchange-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response containing a contract's security definition.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|internal server error, returned when incoming request cannot be processed. It can sometimes include subset of bad requests.  For example, wrong accountId passed and it can only be detected later in handling request. Error contains reason of the problem.<br>|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|service is unavailable. For example if request takes more than 10s due to some internal service unavailability,  request aborted and this status returned<br>|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|

<h3 id="list-all-stock-conids-by-exchange-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» ticker|string|false|none|The ticker symbol of the contract.|
|» conid|integer(int64)|false|none|The contract identifier of the returned contract.|
|» exchange|string|false|none|The primary exchange of the returned contract.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ssoBearer
</aside>

## Modify Allocation Group

<a id="opIdmodifyAllocationGroup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/iserver/account/allocation/group \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Group_1_Shares",
    "prev_name": "Group_0_Shares",
    "default_method": "S",
    "accounts": [
      {
        "name": "U456789",
        "amount": 4
      },
      {
        "name": "U123456",
        "amount": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/api/iserver/account/allocation/group`

Modify an existing allocation group.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Group_1_Shares",
  "prev_name": "Group_0_Shares",
  "default_method": "S",
  "accounts": [
    {
      "name": "U456789",
      "amount": 4
    },
    {
      "name": "U123456",
      "amount": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="modify-allocation-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Name used to refer to your allocation group. If prev_name is specified, this will become the new name of the group.|
|» prev_name|body|string|false|Can be used to rename a group. Using this field will recognize the previous name, while the "name" filed will mark the updated name.|
|» accounts|body|[object]|true|An array of accounts that should be held in the allocation group and, if using a User-specified allocaiton method, the value correlated to the allocation.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The accountId of a given sub-account.|
|» » amount|body|integer(int64)|false|The total distribution value for each sub-account for user-defined allocation methods.|
|» default_method|body|[allocationMethod](#schemaallocationmethod)|true|Interactive Brokers supports two forms of allocation methods. Allocation methods that have calculations completed by Interactive Brokers, and a set of allocation methods calculated by the user and then specified. IB-computed allocation methods:<br>  * `A` - Available Equity<br>  * `E` - Equal<br>  * `N` - Net Liquidation Value<br><br>User-specified allocation methods:<br>  * `C` - Cash Quantity<br>  * `P` - Percentage<br>  * `R` - Ratios<br>  * `S` - Shares<br>|

|Parameter|Value|

|» default_method|E|
|» default_method|N|

|» default_method|P|
|» default_method|R|
|» default_method|S|

```json
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

```json
  "error": "string"
}
```

```json
  "error": "string",
  "statusCode": 0
}
```

`POST /v1/api/iserver/account/allocation/presets`

Set the preset behavior for new allocation groups for specific events.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "group_auto_close_positions": true,
  "default_method_for_all": "AvailableEquity",
  "profiles_auto_close_positions": true,
  "strict_credit_check": true,
  "group_proportional_allocation": true
}
```

<h3 id="set-allocation-preset-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[presets](#schemapresets)|true|none|
|» group_auto_close_positions|body|boolean|false|Determines if allocation groups should prioritize closing positions over equal distribution.|
|» default_method_for_all|body|string|false|Interactive Brokers supports two forms of allocation methods. Allocation methods that have calculations completed by Interactive Brokers, and a set of allocation methods calculated by the user and then specified. IB-computed allocation methods:<br>  * `A` - Available Equity<br>  * `E` - Equal<br>  * `N` - Net Liquidation Value<br><br>User-specified allocation methods:<br>  * `C` - Cash Quantity<br>  * `P` - Percentage<br>  * `R` - Ratios<br>  * `S` - Shares<br>|
|» profiles_auto_close_positions|body|boolean|false|Determines if allocation profiles should prioritize closing positions over equal distribution.|
|» strict_credit_check|body|boolean|false|Determines if the system should always check user credit before beginning the order process every time, or only at the time of order placement and execution.|
|» group_proportional_allocation|body|boolean|false|Determines if the system should keep allocation groups proportional for scaling.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» default_method_for_all|AvailableEquity|
|» default_method_for_all|E|
|» default_method_for_all|N|

## Invest Account Into Model

<a id="opIdsetAccountinvestmentInModel"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/fa/model/invest-divest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reqID": 0,
    "model": "string",
    "accountList": [
      {
        "account": "string",
        "amtToInvest": 0
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/fa/model/invest-divest`

Submit invest or divest instructions for one or more accounts into a **single** destination model, with a **per-account** cash amount. Each entry in `accountList` pairs an account identifier with the individual `amtToInvest` value applied to that account (positive to invest, negative to divest).

Constraints and comparison to `/fa/model/tws-invest-divest`:
 * Only a **single model** may be targeted per request (the top-level `model`
   field). To invest into multiple models in one call, use
   `/fa/model/tws-invest-divest` and its `modelList`.
 * The model must be denominated in a **single currency**; multi-currency
   models are not supported by this endpoint. Use `/fa/model/tws-invest-divest`
   for models holding instruments across multiple currencies.
 * FA pre-trade allocation **groups are not supported** here â€” each account
   and its individual investment amount must be listed explicitly in
   `accountList`.
 * Because each account is listed individually, this endpoint allows a
   **different investment amount per account**. `/fa/model/tws-invest-divest`,
   by contrast, splits a single `amtToInvest` equally across accounts when a
   `group` or `accountList` is used.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reqID": 0,
  "model": "string",
  "accountList": [
    {
      "account": "string",
      "amtToInvest": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="invest-account-into-model-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reqID|body|integer(int64)|false|Request identifier to uniquely track a request.|
|» model|body|string|false|Define the model to invest accounts into.|
|» accountList|body|[object]|false|Collection of accounts to invest in a model.|
|» » account|body|string|false|Account identifier to invest.|
|» » amtToInvest|body|number|false|Amount of cash to invest in the model from the account.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "reqID": "130",
  "subscriptionKey": "2",
  "subscriptionStatus": 0
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string"
}
```

> 503 Response

```json
{
  "error": "string",
  "statusCode": 0
}
```

|200|OK|Successfully submitted model investment.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|internal server error, returned when incoming request cannot be processed. It can sometimes include subset of bad requests.  For example, wrong accountId passed and it can only be detected later in handling request. Error contains reason of the problem.<br>|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|service is unavailable. For example if request takes more than 10s due to some internal service unavailability,  request aborted and this status returned<br>|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» sortField|body|string|false|Field to sort the response by.<br>  * `actual` - Current actual model allocation for the instrument.<br>  * `actualRangeMax` - Maximum actual model allocation allowed for the instrument.<br>  * `actualRangeMin` - Minimum actual model allocation allowed for the instrument.<br>  * `ccy` - Currency of the instrument.<br>  * `conid` - Contract identifier, or conid.<br>  * `dlv` - Market value.<br>  * `instrumentImbalance` - How far an instrument's actual allocation is from its model.<br>  * `instrument` - Symbol of the security.<br>  * `mv` - Market value of the model position.<br>  * `position` - Number of shares held by the model.<br>  * `target` - Target percentage of an instrument held within a model.<br>|
|» sortDirection|body|string|false|Direction to sort the request by.<br> * `ASC` - Sort from greatest to smallest.<br> * `DESC` - Sort from smallest to greatest.<br>|
|» limit|body|integer(int64)|false|Maximum number of positions to return.|

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/fa/model/rebalance/to-new-targets`

Rebalance the specified model to a brand-new set of target position and cash allocations supplied on the request. The full replacement target set is submitted; the response returns a subscription key for polling the resulting allocation preview.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reqID": 398896,
  "model": "Sample-Model",
  "positionTargets": [
    {
      "conid": 1715006,
      "target": 0,
      "locked": true
    }
  ],
  "cashTargets": [
    {
      "ccy": "USD",
      "target": 0,
      "locked": true
    }
  ],
  "subscriptionKey": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reqID|body|integer(int64)|true|Request identifier to uniquely track a request.|
|» model|body|string|true|Name of the model to rebalance.|
|» positionTargets|body|[object]|true|Full replacement list of position targets for the model.|
|» » conid|body|integer(int64)|false|Contract identifier for the instrument to target.|
|» » target|body|number|false|Target allocation for the instrument, expressed as a fraction of the model (e.g. `0.3` = 30%).|
|» » locked|body|boolean|false|Whether the target is locked and should not be adjusted by the rebalancer.|
|» cashTargets|body|[object]|true|Full replacement list of currency cash targets for the model.|
|» » ccy|body|string|false|Currency code of the cash target (ISO 4217).|
|» » target|body|number|false|Target allocation for the currency, expressed as a fraction of the model.|
|» » locked|body|boolean|false|Whether the cash target is locked and should not be adjusted by the rebalancer.|
|» subscriptionKey|body|string|false|Subscription key returned by a prior polling response. Send an empty string on the initial request; supply the returned key on follow-up poll requests.<br>|

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Rebalance To Specific Targets

<a id="opIdrebalanceToSpecificTargets"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/fa/model/rebalance/to-specific-targets \
  -X POST \

      }
    ],

  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/fa/model/rebalance/to-specific-targets`

Rebalance the specified model by overriding only the supplied position targets, leaving all other model targets unchanged. Unlike `to-new-targets`, this endpoint returns the fully computed allocation preview inline (allocations, allocation totals, transfer plan, and warnings/errors) rather than a subscription key.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reqID": 398899,
  "model": "MODEL-API-DEMO",
  "positionTargets": [
    {
      "conid": 268084,
      "target": 0,
      "locked": true
    }
  ],
  "subscriptionKey": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="rebalance-to-specific-targets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reqID|body|integer(int64)|true|Request identifier to uniquely track a request.|
|» model|body|string|true|Name of the model to rebalance.|
|» positionTargets|body|[object]|true|Position targets to override for the model. Only these instruments are adjusted; the rest of the model is preserved.|
|» » conid|body|integer(int64)|false|Contract identifier for the instrument to target.|
|» » target|body|number|false|Target allocation for the instrument, expressed as a fraction of the model.|
|» » locked|body|boolean|false|Whether the target is locked and should not be adjusted by the rebalancer.|
|» subscriptionKey|body|string|false|Subscription key. Send an empty string on the initial request.|

## TWS Invest / Divest

<a id="opIdtwsInvestDivest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/fa/model/tws-invest-divest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "reqID": 398889,
    "account": "DU12349",
    "accountList": [
      "DU12349",
      "DU12350",
      "DU12351"
    ],
    "group": "Group1",
    "modelList": [
      {
        "investCurrency": "USD",
        "amtToInvest": 1000,
        "model": "MODEL-API-DEMO"
      }
    ],
    "subscriptionKey": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/fa/model/tws-invest-divest`

Submit TWS-style invest or divest instructions across **one or more destination models** for a set of accounts. Positive `amtToInvest` values invest cash into the target model; negative values divest. The response returns the resulting allocation plan and cash transfers between the source cash pool and each destination model.

The set of accounts to invest can be specified in one of three **mutually exclusive** ways:
 * `account` - a single U-account identifier
   (e.g. `"account": "DU12349"`).
 * `accountList` - an explicit list of U-account identifiers
   (e.g. `"accountList": ["DU12349", "DU12350", "DU12351"]`).
 * `group` - the name of an FA pre-trade allocation group
   (e.g. `"group": "Group1"`), or `"All"` to include every account under the
   advisor. When `accountList` or `group` is used, each `amtToInvest` value is
   **divided equally** across the resolved accounts.


Feature comparison vs. `/fa/model/invest-divest`:
 * `tws-invest-divest` supports models denominated in **multiple currencies**;
   `invest-divest` supports only single-currency models.
 * `tws-invest-divest` accepts **multiple destination models** per request
   (via `modelList`); `invest-divest` targets a single model per request.
 * `invest-divest` allows a **different investment amount per account**
   because each account is listed individually with its own `amtToInvest`.
   FA pre-trade allocation groups are not supported by `invest-divest`.
 * When `tws-invest-divest` uses `group` or `accountList`, the single
   `amtToInvest` is split **equally** across all resolved accounts.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "reqID": 398889,
  "account": "DU12349",
  "accountList": [
    "DU12349",
    "DU12350",
    "DU12351"
  ],
  "group": "Group1",
  "modelList": [
    {
      "investCurrency": "USD",
      "amtToInvest": 1000,
      "model": "MODEL-API-DEMO"
    }
  ],
  "subscriptionKey": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="tws-invest-divest-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» reqID|body|integer(int64)|true|Request identifier to uniquely track a request.|
|» account|body|string|false|Single U-account identifier submitting the invest/divest instructions. Mutually exclusive with `accountList` and `group`.<br>|
|» accountList|body|[string]|false|Explicit list of U-account identifiers to invest/divest. Each `amtToInvest` value in `modelList` is divided equally across the listed accounts. Mutually exclusive with `account` and `group`.<br>|
|» group|body|string|false|Name of an FA pre-trade allocation group whose member accounts should receive the invest/divest instructions. Use `"All"` to target every account under the advisor. When supplied, each `amtToInvest` value in `modelList` is divided equally across the resolved group members. Mutually exclusive with `account` and `accountList`.<br>|
|» modelList|body|[object]|true|List of invest/divest instructions, one per model destination.|
|» » investCurrency|body|string|false|Currency (ISO 4217) of the invest/divest amount.|
|» » amtToInvest|body|number|false|Amount of cash to invest into the model. Use a negative value to divest.|
|» » model|body|string|false|Destination model for the invest/divest instruction.|
|» subscriptionKey|body|string|false|Subscription key. Send an empty string on the initial request.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "allocations": [
    {
      "account": "DU12345",
      "batchNumber": 4,
      "cashQty": "15.73",
      "closePosition": false,
      "conid": 270639,
      "isCashQty": false,
      "model": "MODEL-API-DEMO",
      "price": "103.256",
      "quantity": "0.1523",
      "relatedRequestAccount": "DU12345",
      "relatedRequestID": "21449",
      "secType": "STK"
    },
    {
      "account": "DU12345",
      "batchNumber": 4,
      "cashQty": "206.92",
      "closePosition": false,
      "conid": 76792991,
      "isCashQty": false,
      "model": "MODEL-API-DEMO",
      "price": "339.489",
      "quantity": "0.6095",
      "relatedRequestAccount": "DU12345",
      "relatedRequestID": "21449",
      "secType": "STK"
    }
  ],
  "cashTransfers": [
    {
      "account": "DU12345",
      "amt": "3000",
      "batchNumber": 1,
      "ccy": "USD",
      "destinationModel": "MODEL-API-DEMO",
      "sourceModel": "Core"
    }
  ],
  "errors": "None",

  "reqID": 398889,

  "transfersInstructionId": 2
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

```bash
        "orderType": "MKT",

        "price": 0,

        "ticker": "AAPL",
        "tif": "DAY",

        "strategy": "string",
        "strategyParameters": {}
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/iserver/account/{modelCode}/orders`

Create Model Portfolio invest or rebalancing order. Submits one or more order instructions against the Model Portfolio identified by `modelCode` in the URL path. Each order entry follows the standard IBKR order submission contract used by `/iserver/account/{accountId}/orders`, with `acctId` set to the target sub-account and orders routed under the model.

This endpoint returns either a list of successfully submitted order confirmations or a list of reply objects that require follow-up confirmation via `/iserver/reply/{replyId}` before the orders are transmitted.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "orders": [
    {
      "acctId": "DU12345",
      "conid": 265598,
      "conidex": "265598@SMART",
      "secType": "STK",
      "cOID": "my-model-order-001",
      "parentId": "string",
      "orderType": "MKT",
      "listingExchange": "SMART",
      "isSingleGroup": true,
      "outsideRTH": true,
      "price": 0,
      "auxPrice": 0,
      "side": "BUY",
      "ticker": "AAPL",
      "tif": "DAY",
      "trailingAmt": 0,
      "trailingType": "amt",
      "referrer": "ModelPortfolio",
      "quantity": 100,
      "cashQty": 0,
      "fxQty": 0,
      "useAdaptive": true,
      "isCcyConv": true,
      "allocationMethod": "AvailableEquity",
      "strategy": "string",
      "strategyParameters": {}
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="submit-new-model-portfolio-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|modelCode|path|string|true|Name of the target Model Portfolio to receive the invest or rebalancing order.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» orders|body|[object]|true|Collection of order instructions to submit against the model portfolio.|
|» » acctId|body|string|false|Sub-account identifier the order applies to under the model.|
|» » conid|body|integer(int64)|false|Contract identifier for the instrument to trade.|
|» » conidex|body|string|false|Combined contract identifier and routing destination in the form `<conid>@<exchange>`. Optional; if omitted, IBKR default routing is used.<br>|
|» » secType|body|string|false|Security type (e.g. `STK`, `OPT`, `FUT`, `CASH`).|
|» » cOID|body|string|false|Client order identifier. Must be unique per order and can be used to correlate submissions with downstream events.<br>|
|» » parentId|body|string|false|`cOID` of the parent order when submitting child orders in a bracket or OCA group.<br>|
|» » orderType|body|string|false|Order type.|
|» » listingExchange|body|string|false|Preferred listing exchange for the instrument.|
|» » isSingleGroup|body|boolean|false|True to submit the order set as a single OCA group.|
|» » outsideRTH|body|boolean|false|True to allow the order to execute outside regular trading hours.|
|» » price|body|number|false|Limit price. Required for `LMT` and `STOP_LIMIT` order types.|
|» » auxPrice|body|number|false|Stop or trailing price. Required for `STP`, `STOP_LIMIT`, and trailing order types.|
|» » side|body|string|false|Order side.|
|» » ticker|body|string|false|Instrument ticker symbol.|
|» » tif|body|string|false|Time in force for the order.|
|» » trailingAmt|body|number|false|Trailing amount for `TRAIL` / `TRAILLMT` order types.|
|» » trailingType|body|string|false|Trailing amount type.|
|» » referrer|body|string|false|Optional referrer identifier used for internal tracking.|
|» » quantity|body|number|false|Share quantity to trade. Mutually exclusive with `cashQty`.|
|» » cashQty|body|number|false|Cash-denominated quantity to trade. Mutually exclusive with `quantity`.|
|» » fxQty|body|number|false|FX quantity for currency conversion orders.|
|» » useAdaptive|body|boolean|false|True to route the order using the IB Adaptive algorithm.|
|» » isCcyConv|body|boolean|false|True if the order is a currency conversion order.|
|» » allocationMethod|body|string|false|FA allocation method used to distribute the order across the model's sub-accounts (e.g. `AvailableEquity`, `NetLiq`, `EqualQuantity`, `PctChange`).<br>|
|» » strategy|body|string|false|Optional algorithmic execution strategy name.|
|» » strategyParameters|body|object|false|Parameters passed to the selected algorithmic strategy.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » orderType|MKT|
|» » orderType|LMT|
|» » orderType|STP|
|» » orderType|STOP_LIMIT|
|» » orderType|MIDPRICE|
|» » orderType|TRAIL|
|» » orderType|TRAILLMT|
|» » side|BUY|
|» » side|SELL|
|» » tif|DAY|
|» » tif|GTC|
|» » tif|OPG|
|» » tif|IOC|
|» » trailingType|amt|
|» » trailingType|%|

> Example responses

```json
[
  {
    "order_id": "1799115492",
    "order_status": "PreSubmitted",
    "encrypt_message": "1"
  }
]
```

|200|OK|Successfully submitted the model portfolio order(s). The response is either a list of order confirmations, or a list of reply objects requiring follow-up confirmation via `/iserver/reply/{replyId}`.<br>|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Missing, empty, non-numeric, or out-of-range parameter. The `error` field is always prefixed with `Bad Request:`.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|

For example, wrong accountId passed and it can only be detected later in handling request. Error contains reason of the problem.<br>|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|service is unavailable. For example if request takes more than 10s due to some internal service unavailability,  request aborted and this status returned<br>|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|

<h3 id="submit-new-model-portfolio-order-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

## List Allocation Models

<a id="opIdgetAllocationModels"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/iserver/account/allocation/models \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/api/iserver/account/allocation/models`

Retrieve the list of allocation model portfolios available under the authenticated Financial Advisor account. Each response entry is keyed by the model name and its value is a delimited string containing the master account identifier, model name, and internal model designator/flag tokens separated by the `\x1d` (ASCII group separator) character.

**IMPORTANT:** Ensure this endpoint is queried **first**, prior to accessing any other Model Portfolio resources in the Web API. The model list returned here primes the session's model context and is required before subsequent Model Portfolio endpoints (model summary, positions, invest/divest, rebalance, order submission, etc.) will return correct results.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "Sample-Model": "DF123456\\x1dSample-Model\\x1dM\\x1dT",
  "Technology": "DF123456\\x1dTechnology\\x1dM\\x1dT",
  "Industrials": "DF123456\\x1dIndustrials\\x1dM\\x1dT",
  "GlobalStocks": "DF123456\\x1dGlobalStocks\\x1dM\\x1dT",
  "MODEL-API-DEMO": "DF123456\\x1dMODEL-API-DEMO\\x1dM\\x1dT"
}
```

```json
{
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "statusCode": 401
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## Historical OHLC Bar Data

<a id="opIdgetMdHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/iserver/marketdata/history?conid=265598&period=6d&bar=5min' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/api/iserver/marketdata/history`

Request historical data for an instrument in the form of OHLC bars.

<h3 id="historical-ohlc-bar-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|conid|query|integer(int64)|true|IB contract ID of the requested instrument.|
|period|query|string|true|A time duration away from startTime into the future to be divided into bars of the specified width. Supported Period Sizes<br>  * `min` - Minutes<br>  * `h` - Hour(s)<br>  * `d` - Day(s)<br>  * `w` - Week(s)<br>  * `m` - Month(s)<br>  * `y` - Year(s)<br>|
|bar|query|string|true|The width of the bars into which the interval determined by period and startTime will be divided. It is not required that bar evenly divide period; partial bars can be returned. Supported Bar Sizes<br>  * `S` - Second(s)<br>  * `min` - Minute(s)<br>  * `h` - Hour(s)<br>  * `d` - Day(s)<br>  * `w` - Week(s)<br>  * `m` - Month(s)<br>|
|exchange|query|string|false|Exchange (or SMART) from which data is requested.|
|outsideRth|query|boolean|false|Indicates whether data outside of regular trading hours should be included in response.|
|startTime|query|[utcDateTime](#schemautcdatetime)|false|A fixed UTC date-time reference point for the historical data request, from which the specified period extends. Format is YYYYMMDD-hh:mm:ss. If omitted, the current time is used, and direction must be omitted or 1.|
|direction|query|integer(int64)|false|Indicates whether data should begin or end at the start time.<br>  * `-1` - Historical data will begin away from the start time, ending at the current time/startTime.<br>  * `1` - Historical data begins at the start time, moving towards the current time. Only supported when startTime is included.<br>|
|source|query|string|false|The type of data to be returned in the historical bars. Supported Bar Sizes<br>  * `Bid_Ask` - The OHLC bid/ask values.<br>  * `Last` - The OHLC trade values.<br>  * `Midpoint` - The OHLC of the Bid-Ask midpoint.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|direction|-1|
|direction|1|

<h3 id="modify-open-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|path|string|true|The account to which the order will clear.|
|orderId|path|string|true|The IB-assigned order ID of the desired order ticket.|
|body|body|[singleOrderSubmissionRequest](#schemasingleordersubmissionrequest)|true|none|
|» acctId|body|string|false|Receiving account of the order ticket.|
|» conid|body|integer(int64)|true|IB contract ID of the instrument.|
|» conidex|body|string|false|Contract ID and routing destination together in format 123456@EXCHANGE.|
|» secType|body|string|false|IB asset class identifier.|
|» cOID|body|string|false|Client-configurable order identifier. The value must be unique for a 24 hour span. The value can be no longer than 64 characters. Should not be set for the child of a bracket order.<br>|
|» parentId|body|string|false|If the order ticket is a child order in a bracket, the parentId field must be set equal to the cOID provided for the parent order.|
|» listingExchange|body|string|false|The listing exchange of the instrument.|
|» isSingleGroup|body|boolean|false|Indicates that all orders in the containing array are to be treated as an OCA group.|
|» outsideRTH|body|boolean|false|Instructs IB to permit the order to execute outside of regular trading hours.|
|» allOrNone|body|boolean|false|Instructs IB to execute the order  entirely or not execute at all.|
|» auxPrice|body|number|false|Additional price value used in certain order types, such as stop orders.|
|» ticker|body|string|false|Ticker symbol of the instrument.|
|» trailingAmt|body|number|false|Offset used with Trailing orders.|
|» trailingType|body|string|false|Specifies the type of trailing used with a Trailing order.|
|» referrer|body|string|false|IB internal identifier for order entry UI element.|
|» cashQty|body|number|false|Quantity of currency used with cash quantity orders.|
|» useAdaptive|body|boolean|false|Instructs IB to apply the Price Management Algo.|
|» isCcyConv|body|boolean|false|Indicates that a forex order is for currency conversion and should not entail a virtual forex position in the account, where applicable.|
|» orderType|body|string|true|IB order type identifier.|
|» price|body|number|false|Price of the order ticket, where applicable.|
|» side|body|string|true|Side of the order ticket.|
|» tif|body|string|true|Time in force of the order ticket.|
|» quantity|body|number|true|Quantity of the order ticket in units of the instrument.|
|» strategy|body|string|false|The name of an execution algorithm.|
|» strategyParameters|body|object|false|Parameters governing the selected algorithm, if applicable.|
|» » PLACEHOLDER|body|string|false|Placeholder -- these vary by algo (and not always type string, sometimes bool)|
|» extOperator|body|string|false|ExtOperator is used to identify external operator|
|» manualIndicator|body|boolean|false|For all orders for US Futures products, clients must submit this flag to indicate whether the order was originated manually (by a natural person) or automatically (by an automated trading system transmitting orders without human intervention). Submit a True value to indicate a manually originated order, and submit a False value to indicate an automated order. Orders for USFUT products that do not include this field will be rejected.|

|replyId|path|string|true|The UUID of the reply message to be confirmed, obtained from an order submission response. This is delivered from the POST /iserver/account/{accountId}/orders endpoint when triggering certain warning messages. <br>|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» confirmed|body|boolean|false|Value of true answers the question in the affirmative and proceeds with order submission.|

```json
  "statusCode": 0
}
```

<h3 id="confirm-order-reply-message-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Status of reply|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|internal server error, returned when incoming request cannot be processed. It can sometimes include subset of bad requests.  For example, wrong accountId passed and it can only be detected later in handling request. Error contains reason of the problem.<br>|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|service is unavailable. For example if request takes more than 10s due to some internal service unavailability,  request aborted and this status returned<br>|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|

<h3 id="confirm-order-reply-message-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[orderSubmitSuccess](#schemaordersubmitsuccess)|false|none|A successful submission of one or more order tickets.|
|*oneOf*|[orderReplyMessage](#schemaorderreplymessage)|false|none|An array containing objects that each deliver the order reply messages emitted against one order ticket in the submission request's array.  Indicies of the order reply message objects in this array correspond to the indicies of the order tickets in the submission request's array.<br>|
|*oneOf*|[orderSubmitError](#schemaordersubmiterror)|false|none|Indicates that the order reply message or submission was not accepted.|
|*oneOf*|[orderReplyNotFound](#schemaorderreplynotfound)|false|none|Indicates that the order reply ID does not exist.|
|*oneOf*|[advancedOrderReject](#schemaadvancedorderreject)|false|none|Relates a message generated in response to the rejection of the submitted order ticket. In some cases, it may also present a mechanism to resubmit the same order following a prompted decision.|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ssoBearer
</aside>

## Portfolio Subaccounts (Large Account Structures)

<a id="opIdgetManySubaccounts"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/portfolio/subaccounts2 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/api/portfolio/subaccounts2`

Used in tiered account structures (such as Financial Advisor and IBroker Accounts) to return a list of sub-accounts, paginated up to 1000 accounts per page, for which the user can view position and account-related information.  This endpoint must be called prior to calling other /portfolio endpoints for those sub-accounts. If you have less than 100 sub-accounts use /portfolio/subaccounts.  To query a list of accounts the user can trade, see /iserver/accounts.


<h3 id="portfolio-subaccounts-large-account-structures-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|path|string|true|none|

|page|query|integer(int64)|false|none|
|pageSize|query|integer(int64)|false|none|

<h3 id="account-positions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|positions|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Missing, empty, non-numeric, or out-of-range parameter. The `error` field is always prefixed with `Bad Request:`.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|internal server error, returned when incoming request cannot be processed. It can sometimes include subset of bad requests.  For example, wrong accountId passed and it can only be detected later in handling request. Error contains reason of the problem.<br>|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|service is unavailable. For example if request takes more than 10s due to some internal service unavailability,  request aborted and this status returned<br>|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|

<h3 id="account-positions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[individualPosition](#schemaindividualposition)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
ssoBearer
</aside>

## Account Portfolio Summary

<a id="opIdgetPortfolioSummary"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/portfolio/DU123456/summary \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/api/portfolio/{accountId}/summary`

Returns detailed summary of account values, by segment where appropriate.

<h3 id="account-portfolio-summary-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|path|string|true|none|
|model|query|string|false|none|

## Account Positions (NEW)

<a id="opIdgetUncachedPositions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/portfolio2/DU123456/positions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v1/api/portfolio2/{accountId}/positions`

Returns a list of positions for the given account. /v1/api/portfolio/accounts or /portfolio/subaccounts must be called prior to this endpoint. This endpoint provides near-real time updates and removes caching otherwise found in the /portfolio/{accountId}/positions/{pageId} endpoint.


<h3 id="account-positions-new-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accountId|path|string|true|none|
|model|query|string|false|none|
|direction|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|a|
|direction|d|

> Example responses

```json

]
```

<h1 id="ib-rest-api-trading-portfolio-analyst">Trading Portfolio Analyst</h1>

## Portfolio Allocation

<a id="opIdcreateAllocation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/pa/allocation \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "acctIds": [
      "DU123456"
    ],
    "type": "FINANCIAL_INSTRUMENT",
    "currency": "USD",
    "date": "string",
    "model": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/pa/allocation`

Returns consolidated portfolio allocation by Financial Instrument, Asset Class, Sector, Region, or Country for a given set of accounts. Result is aggregated for the included accounts. Current day data is supported only if all included accounts have the same base currency as specified in the currency parameter.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acctIds": [
    "DU123456"
  ],
  "type": "FINANCIAL_INSTRUMENT",
  "currency": "USD",
  "date": "string",
  "model": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="portfolio-allocation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» acctIds|body|[string]|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The allocation category type. One of FINANCIAL_INSTRUMENT, ASSET_CLASS, SECTOR, REGION, COUNTRY, or ALL. Case insensitive. When ALL is specified, the response includes allocations for every category type.<br>|
|» currency|body|string|false|Three character currency code. The base currency to use for the NAV calculation in the response.<br>|
|» date|body|string|false|Optional. Formatted as yyyymmdd. If specified, should be prior to the current day. If not specified, request will be for the current day. If the request is for current day and current day data is not available, then the response will be for the previous business day.<br>|
|» model|body|string|false|Optional. Model portfolio name to use for the allocation calculation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|FINANCIAL_INSTRUMENT|
|» type|ASSET_CLASS|
|» type|SECTOR|
|» type|REGION|
|» type|COUNTRY|
|» type|ALL|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "getAllocation",
  "currency": "USD",
  "realtime": false,
  "date": "20240611",
  "allocations": {
```

|401|Unauthorized|Missing, invalid, or unparseable Authorization token.|[ErrorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|internal server error, returned when incoming request cannot be processed. It can sometimes include subset of bad requests.  For example, wrong accountId passed and it can only be detected later in handling request. Error contains reason of the problem.<br>|[errorOnlyResponse](#schemaerroronlyresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|service is unavailable. For example if request takes more than 10s due to some internal service unavailability,  request aborted and this status returned<br>|[errorResponse](#schemaerrorresponse-1)|

## Account Performance (All Time Periods)

<a id="opIdgetPerformanceAllPeriods"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/pa/allperiods \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "acctIds": [
      "[\"DU123456\"]"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/api/pa/allperiods`

Returns the performance (MTM) for the given accounts, if more than one account is passed, the result is consolidated.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "acctIds": [
    "[\"DU123456\"]"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="account-performance-all-time-periods-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|param|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» acctIds|body|[string]|false|An array of strings containing each account identifier to retrieve performance details for.|
